source.title: Open problems on structure of positively curved projective varieties

accepted.question_text: Let X be a projective variety with mild singularities, for example klt singularities. An MRC fibration is a rational map φ: X ⇢ Y whose general fibers are compact and rationally connected and such that no horizontal rational curve passes through a very general point of X; the birational model of the base Y is not uniquely determined. Under what conditions can one choose the birational model Y so that the MRC fibration is represented by a holomorphic map rather than only an almost holomorphic rational map?

evidence.quote: A rational map φ : X ⇢ Y is called an RC fibration (resp. MRC fibration) if it satisfies the first two conditions (resp. all the conditions) below:
General fibers of φ : X ⇢ Y are rationally connected.
There is no horizontal rational curve (i.e., no rational curve whose image under φ is not one point) passing through a very general point in X.
Problem 2.1. — When do we choose an MRC fibration to be holomorphic from the ambiguities in the choices of Y ?

accepted.question_text: If X is a compact Kähler manifold with positive holomorphic sectional curvature, must X be projective and rationally connected?
accepted.context_brief: Yau conjecture on positive holomorphic sectional curvature

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 (Yau’s conjecture, [54, Problem 47]). — If a compact Kähler manifold X has positive holomorphic sectional curvature, then X is projective and rationally connected.
Yang in [51] solved Yau’s conjecture by introducing the notion of the RC positivity

accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact Kähler manifold with Kähler metric g of semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For p in X, let V_flat,p be the subspace of T_X,p consisting of tangent vectors v such that R_g(v,x,y,z̄)=0 for every x,y,z in T_X,p, and define ntf(X,g)=dim X−inf_p dim V_flat,p. If φ: X ⇢ Y is an MRC fibration in the same rationally connected sense as for projective varieties, does the inequality dim X−dim Y ≥ ntf(X,g), known in the smooth projective case, still hold in the compact Kähler setting?
accepted.context_brief: Kähler extension of the ntf inequality

evidence.quote: The invariant ntf(X, g) can be seen as an analog of the numerical Kodaira dimension (see [43] for the definition) and measures the positivity of holomorphic sectional curvatures.
Let X be a smooth projective variety and g be a Kähler metric with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Let φ : X ⇢ Y be an MRC fibration of X. Then we obtain dim X − dim Y ⩾ ntf(X, g).
This theorem is expected to still hold in the case where X is a compact Kähler manifold.

accepted.question_text: Let (X,g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For p in X, let V_flat,p be the subspace of T_X,p consisting of tangent vectors v such that R_g(v,x,y,z̄)=0 for every x,y,z in T_X,p, and define ntf(X,g)=dim X−inf_p dim V_flat,p. If ntf(X,g)=dim X, must H^0(X, Ω_X^q)=0 for every q>0, and must X be projective?

evidence.quote: Here a tangent vector v ∈ TX,p at a point p ∈ X is said to be truly flat if it satisfies that Rg(v, x, y, z̄) = 0 for any x, y, z ∈ TX,p.

Problem 3.3 ([39, Problem 5.1]). — Let (X, g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Assume that ntf(X, g) = dim X. • Does it hold that h0(X, ΩqX)=0 for any q > 0? • Is X automatically projective?

accepted.question_text: Can the smooth-projective structure theorem for varieties with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature be extended to compact Kähler manifolds? In concrete terms, should such a compact Kähler manifold admit a locally trivial MRC fibration φ: X → Y to a flat base Y, with rationally connected fiber F; after a finite étale cover A → Y by an abelian variety, should the pullback X* = A ×_Y X have a locally trivial Albanese map to A; should the universal cover split as ℂ^m × F; and should the fundamental group be an extension of a finite group by a free abelian group?
accepted.context_brief: Structure theorem for compact Kähler manifolds

evidence.quote: The morphism φ : X → Y is a locally trivial morphism.
The image Y is a smooth projective variety with a flat metric.
The fiber F is a rationally connected manifold. In particular, the morphism φ : X → Y is an MRC fibration of X.
We obtain an isomorphism Xuniv ∼= Cm × F, where Xuniv is the universal cover of X, and F is the rationally connected fiber of φ.
In particular, the fundamental group of X is an extension of a finite group by Z⊕2m.
It is an attractive problem to generalize the above structure theorem to compact Kähler manifolds. Problem 3.5. — Can we generalize Theorem 3.4 to compact Kähler manifolds?

accepted.question_text: Let (X,g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Is the fundamental group of X an extension of a finite group by ℤ^{2m}? After replacing X by an appropriate finite étale cover X* and considering the Albanese map α: X* → Alb(X*) with fiber F, does F admit a Kähler metric g_F such that ntf(F,g_F)=dim F, and is F projective and rationally connected?

evidence.quote: The same conclusion can be expected even when X is a compact Kähler manifold, but it is still an open problem.
Problem 3.6 (cf. [39, Problem 5.2]). — Let (X, g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature.
Is the fundamental group of X is an extension of a finite group by Z⊕2m?
Does the fiber F admit a Kähler metric gF such that ntf(F, gF ) = dim F?
Is the fiber F projective and rationally connected?

accepted.question_text: Let (X,g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive or semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature. Let V be the set of appropriate truly flat tangent vectors, where a truly flat tangent vector v at p satisfies R_g(v,x,y,z̄)=0 for all x,y,z in T_X,p. Does V determine an integrable subbundle of T_X, and can one find a complementary subbundle W with T_X ≅ W ⊕ V? In the semi-positive case, can this splitting construct an MRC fibration f: X → Y with W equal to the relative tangent bundle T_{X/Y}; in the semi-negative case, can it construct the Iitaka fibration f: X → Z associated with K_X with V equal to T_{X/Z}?
accepted.context_brief: Truly flat tangent vectors and fibrations

evidence.quote: Here a tangent vector v ∈ TX,p at a point p ∈ X is said to be truly flat if it satisfies that Rg(v, x, y, z̄) = 0 for any x, y, z ∈ TX,p.
Problem 3.7. — Let (X, g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive (or semi-negative) holomorphic sectional curvature. Let V ⊂ TX be the set of “appropriate” truly flat tangent vectors.
Does V determine an integrable subbundle of TX?
Can we find a subbundle W ⊂ TX such that TX ∼= W ⊕ V ?
In the case of semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvatures, can we construct an MRC fibration f : X → Y such that W = TX/Y ?
In the case of semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvatures, can we construct the Iitaka fibration f : X → Z associated with the canonical bundle KX such that V = TX/Z?

accepted.question_text: Does the blow-up of a Hirzebruch surface admit positive holomorphic sectional curvature? More broadly, can all varieties of a fixed dimension, for example surfaces or threefolds, with semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature be classified, and can one identify an algebraic-geometric analogue of semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature?
accepted.context_brief: Classification under positive holomorphic sectional curvature

evidence.quote: The complete classification is not known even in the case of surfaces.
It is not even obvious whether the blow-up of Hirzebruch surfaces has a positive holomorphic sectional curvature.
Problem 3.8 (cf. [39, Problem 5.3]). —
Does the blow-up of Hirzebruch surfaces admit a positive holomorphic sectional curvature?
Can we classify all the varieties of fixed dimension (e.g., dimension two or three) with semi-positive (or positive) holomorphic sectional curvature?
Can we find an analog of semi-positive (or positive) holomorphic sectional curvatures in algebraic geometry?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective variety whose tangent bundle T_X is pseudo-effective, meaning equivalently that there is an ample line bundle A such that A ⊗ Sym^m(T_X) is generically globally generated for every m>0, or that the non-nef locus of O_{P(T_X)}(1) is not dominant over X. The known structure theorem gives a holomorphic MRC fibration φ: X → Y to a smooth projective variety Y. Is this MRC fibration locally trivial?
accepted.context_brief: Local triviality for pseudo-effective tangent bundles

evidence.quote: There exists an ample line bundle A such that A⊗Symm E is generically globally generated for any integer m > 0 (i.e., A ⊗ Symm E is generated by global sections at a general point).
The non-nef locus of OP(E)(1) is not dominant over X.
Theorem 4.2 ([35, Theorem 1.1]). — Let X be a smooth projective variety with pseudo-effective tangent bundle. Then X admits a holomorphic MRC fibration φ : X → Y to a smooth projective variety Y
Problem 4.3. — Let X be a smooth projective variety with pseudo-effective tangent bundle. Then is the MRC fibration φ : X → Y locally trivial?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a rationally connected manifold whose tangent bundle T_X is pseudo-effective in the sense that some ample line bundle A makes A ⊗ Sym^m(T_X) generically globally generated for every m>0, equivalently the non-nef locus of O_{P(T_X)}(1) is not dominant over X. Must the anti-canonical divisor −K_X be big?

evidence.quote: There exists an ample line bundle A such that A⊗Symm E is generically globally generated for any integer m > 0 (i.e., A ⊗ Symm E is generated by global sections at a general point).
Problem 4.4 ([35, Problem 3.13]). — Let X be a rationally connected manifold with pseudo-effective tangent bundle. Then is the anti-canonical divisor −KX big?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact Kähler manifold with pseudo-effective tangent bundle. After replacing X by an appropriate finite étale cover, consider the Albanese map X → Alb(X) and a fiber F. Can one prove that the anti-canonical divisor −K_F is big or that F is projective? Is the Albanese map itself an MRC fibration of X?
accepted.context_brief: Albanese fibers under pseudo-effective tangent bundle

evidence.quote: Toward structure theorems for compact Kähler manifolds X with pseudo-effective tangent bundle, it was proved in [35, Theorem 3.12] that the Albanese map X → Alb(X) satisfies a similar conclusion to Theorem 4.2. The next problem is to prove the projectivity of fibers.

Problem 4.5. — Let X be a compact Kähler manifold with pseudo-effective tangent bundle. After we replace X with an appropriate finite étale covering of X, we consider the Albanese map X → Alb(X). • Can we prove that the anti-canonical divisor −KF is big or F is projective? • Is the Albanese map X → Alb(X) an MRC fibration of X?

accepted.question_text: Does the blow-up of a Hirzebruch surface at four general points have pseudo-effective tangent bundle, and what can be said about blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces at special points?
accepted.context_brief: Surface examples with pseudo-effective tangent bundle

evidence.quote: The remaining problem in the classification of surfaces is as follows: Problem 4.6. — • Does the blow-up of Hirzebruch surfaces at general four points have the pseudo-effective tangent bundle? • What can we say for the blow-up of Hirzebruch surfaces at special points?

accepted.question_text: Let φ: X ⇢ Y be an almost holomorphic map between smooth projective varieties, let π: Γ → X resolve the indeterminacy locus of φ, and let Γ → Y be the resulting morphism. Suppose there is an effective divisor D on Γ such that (Γ,D) is klt and the Q-divisor −π_*(K_{Γ/Y}+D) is nef. Under this relative anti-canonical assumption, can one obtain a structure theorem? More specifically, after replacing Y by a smooth birational model Y′, can φ be represented by a holomorphic morphism X → Y′ birationally equivalent to the original rational map φ?

evidence.quote: Assume that there exists an effective divisor D on Γ such that (Γ, D) is a klt pair and −π∗(KΓ/Y + D) is a nef Q-divisor.

Problem 5.2. — Under the above assumption for the relative anti-canonical divisor, can we obtain a structure theorem? Specifically, can we choose a holomorphic morphism X → Y′ that is birationally equivalent to the original φ : X ⇢ Y ?

accepted.question_text: What structural restrictions, classification results, or fibration theorems can be established for smooth projective varieties whose anti-canonical divisor −K_X is pseudo-effective? A first concrete direction is to study surjective morphisms φ: X → Y with pseudo-effective relative anti-canonical divisor −K_{X/Y} and determine how that positivity restricts the geometry of φ.

evidence.quote: Proposition 5.3. — What can we say for (smooth) projective varieties with pseudo-effective anti-canonical divisor?
Toward the above problem, it seems to be the first step to consider a surjective morphism φ : X → Y with the pseudo-effective relative anti-canonical −KX/Y .

accepted.question_text: For klt projective pairs (X,Δ) with nef anti-canonical divisor −(K_X+Δ), without assuming that X is smooth, can one establish a structure theorem analogous to the smooth case? In the smooth case the desired structure includes a holomorphic MRC fibration φ: X → Y to a smooth projective variety Y with numerically trivial canonical divisor, local triviality of the pair (X,Δ) over Y, and a universal-cover product decomposition by the universal cover of Y and the typical fiber.
accepted.context_brief: Structure theorem for singular klt pairs

evidence.quote: The most important remaining problem is to establish the structure theorem for klt pairs (X, ∆) with nef anti-canonical divisor −(KX + ∆).

Theorem 5.1 ([10, Theorem 1.3]). — Let (X, ∆) be a klt pair with nef anti-canonical divisor −(KX + ∆). Assume that X is a smooth projective variety. Then there exists a holomorphic MRC fibration φ : X → Y with the following properties:

Moreover, together with the Beauville–Bogomolov decomposition, the universal cover Xuniv of X can be decomposed into the product of rationally connected manifolds, Cm, Calabi–Yau manifolds, hyperkähler manifolds.

accepted.question_text: Let (X,Δ) be a klt pair such that X is smooth and −(K_X+Δ) is nef. Does there exist an orbifold morphism ρ:(X,Δ)→(R,Δ_R) such that (R,Δ_R) is klt, R is smooth, c1(K_R+Δ_R)=0, the general orbifold fibers are slope rationally connected, and the fibration is locally trivial with respect to pairs, meaning that for every small open set U in R the pair (ρ^{-1}(U),Δ) is isomorphic over U to (U,Δ_R|_U)×(X_r,Δ_{X_r}) for a general fiber X_r?

evidence.quote: The MRC fibration is defined only by X, and thus it does not reflect information on the boundary ∆. On the other hand, the slope rationally connected quotient (sRC quotient for short), introduced in [9], gives a generalization of MRC fibrations reflecting the boundary ∆
This conjecture was solved when (X, ∆) is a log smooth surface in [10, Theorem 1.6], but it is still open in the general case.
